display.name: Google Docs
display.summary: Searches and reads the Google Docs shared with your service account, at any folder depth.
examples: Find the onboarding spec and summarise it
Which docs mention the pricing change?
What do the latest meeting notes say about next steps?

fields.label: Service account key
fields.help: The JSON key file of a Google service account. Share the folders you want read with that account's email address.

agent.name: gdocs
agent.description: Searches and reads the Google Docs shared with the service account, at any folder depth: specs, plans, proposals, meeting notes and prose documentation that is not in the repository. A question naming a document without saying which system holds it may be here or in another document store: a filename does not say which, so ask every store.
agent.owns:
You own the shared Google Docs. Search first -- it reaches every document you can see, however deeply nested -- and browse only to orient yourself. You do not own the source repository.

Every document and folder in a listing carries a link. When you report what a document says, GIVE THAT LINK with it: a Drive id is something you pass to read_google_doc, not something a reader can open.

tool_descriptions.browse_drive: List what is in Drive. Call with no folder_id to see what is shared with you, then call it again with a folder's id to see inside that folder. Documents nested in subfolders are only visible by descending into them, so prefer search_docs when you know what you are looking for.
tool_descriptions.search_docs: Find Google Docs whose title or body contains a word or phrase. This searches every document you can reach, however deeply nested, so it is the fastest way to locate material. Returns ids to pass to read_google_doc.
tool_descriptions.read_google_doc: Read one Google Doc's full text by the id shown by search_docs or browse_drive.
